title: TRACE shared contract definitions (v1)
description: Shared $defs used by trace.evidence_bundle/1.0 and trace.intelligence_report/1.0. Frozen at M0. Draft 2020-12. Cross-file $refs are relative and resolve against the $id base https://trace.example/schemas/v1/ (.example is IANA-reserved, RFC 2606).
x-doctrine: Deterministic computation is authoritative. AI is a narrative/reasoning layer only. Confidence is an ordinal reliability figure for a derivation, NOT a probability that a proposition is true.

InstanceId.description: Qualified record identifier. Examples: ART-0001, MED-01, RGRP-03, EVT-0005, CASE-ATLAS-01, BND-MINIMAL-001.

FragmentInstanceId.description: Fragment identifier. Frozen M0 amendment: FRG-<lowercase_hex16>-<start>-<end>. A fragment_id identifies a specific source byte occurrence over the half-open range [start, end) on the fragment's media. The embedded start and end MUST equal the fragment record's byte_range.start and byte_range.end. Identical bytes at different source ranges receive different fragment IDs.

DerivedId.description: Hash-derived identifier. Not sequential. Used only for report_id.

ActionId.description: Recommended-action library code. Examples: ACT-HASH-VERIFY, ACT-MANUAL-REVIEW-RANGE.

VocabCode.description: Open-vocabulary SCREAMING_SNAKE code. Used for warnings[].code and anomalies[].code.

VocabId.description: Open-vocabulary lower_snake identifier. Used for signature_id, marker_id, timestamp source, entropy method, chain-of-custody action.

IsoUtc.description: UTC instant with a mandatory trailing Z. Local offsets such as +05:30 are NOT permitted.

Confidence.description: Ordinal reliability of a derivation, in [0,1]. Comparable only within the same epistemic status. NOT a probability that a proposition is true, and must never be presented or aggregated as one. Ceilings are status-dependent: INFERRED <= 0.70; OBSERVED and COMPUTED <= 1.00, additionally bounded by the monotonicity rule (a derived confidence may not exceed the minimum confidence of the evidence it cites).

ConfidenceCeilings.description: Reported confidence policy. Single source of truth for the AI/authority boundary: only INFERRED carries a numeric cap; the cap exists to express a policy boundary, not a probability.

EpistemicStatus.description: OBSERVED = directly reported by the recovery engine or filesystem/container metadata (non-code synonym: KNOWN). COMPUTED = deterministically derived from OBSERVED inputs by a declared, reproducible rule. INFERRED = interpretation requiring assumptions; AI-permitted but never authoritative. MISSING = cannot be established from available evidence; requires why_missing and what_would_resolve.

ProducedBy.description: Who authored the claim. 'ai' implies status == INFERRED (schema-enforced).

UntrustedText.description: Raw, untrusted, recovered content. C0 controls, ANSI escapes, bidi overrides and instruction-like text are LEGAL here because that is what recovered data looks like. Consumers MUST sanitise before any prompt or render and MUST NEVER treat this content as executable instructions.

SanitizedText.description: Renderable text. C0 controls and DEL are forbidden. The input side (UntrustedText) may be dirty; the output side must be clean.

EvidenceRef.description: MINIMUM reference grammar (M0, frozen). Targets: bundle | case | artifacts[<InstanceId>] | fragments[<FragmentInstanceId>] | reconstruction_groups[<InstanceId>] | timeline_events[<InstanceId>] | known_file_matches[<artifact InstanceId>]. An optional field path of at most two segments may follow, each segment optionally carrying one numeric index (e.g. .timestamps[0]). known_file_matches is the one collection keyed by a foreign identifier (artifact_id). Every EvidenceRef must resolve to exactly one record; unresolvable refs fail grounding.

ArtifactFamily.description: CLOSED vocabulary, frozen for the life of 1.x.

ArtifactKind.description: Fine-grained kind vocabulary used only for fragment type_likelihoods keys. CLOSED, frozen for 1.x.

ArtifactLabel.description: CLOSED classification vocabulary, frozen for 1.x. Free-text labels are rejected. Abstention always maps to 'unknown'.

ByteRange.description: Half-open byte interval [start, end) on the referenced media. Frozen M0 semantics: start >= 0; end > start; size_bytes == end - start when present. Fragment IDs embed start and end and MUST agree with this object. byte_range.start is MEDIA-ABSOLUTE; every other offset nested inside an artifact or fragment record (byte_gaps[].start, strings_sample[].offset, signature_probe.offset_in_fragment) is RELATIVE to the enclosing byte_range.start.

size_bytes.description: Derived: MUST equal end - start when present. Verified by the semantic checker.

ScoreComponent.description: One auditable term of a deterministic score. contribution MUST equal weight * value (semantic rule SM-9); the sum of contributions over a score MUST equal the reported score.

basis_ref.description: Resolution-checked pointer into the evidence bundle.

basis_note.description: Free-text basis when no single bundle path expresses it.

Warning.description: Partial failures MUST be surfaced here rather than by silently omitting data. Identical shape in both documents.

scope.description: Union of the two approved record identifier formats. Not a new ID format.

Claim.description: The claim envelope. Every printable sentence in an intelligence report exists as a Claim. Status, confidence and evidence_refs are deterministic authority; text and alternatives are narrative only.

confidence_basis.description: Required and never empty. This is the primary carrier of derivation reliability, not the number.

evidence_refs.description: Always at least one ref, including for MISSING claims. Use the reserved refs 'bundle' or 'case' for whole-corpus statements.

allOf.x-invariant: INV-SE-1: AI is never authoritative. produced_by == 'ai' implies status == INFERRED.
INV-SE-2: truth is deterministic. OBSERVED/COMPUTED imply produced_by == 'deterministic'.
INV-SE-4: every gap must be actionable.
